subject: Re: Redwood integration — rate limits, retries, and idempotency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme discovery call — integration recap & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

Recap:
- Primary goal: embed Redwood inference into Acme's product search pipeline for better relevance and faster reranking.
- Key integration areas we covered: SDK setup, auth (service account vs API key for server-side calls), routing (region and fallback policies), structured output / tool calling for enrichment, and embeddings + reranker strategy.
- Non-functional requirements: target 95th percentile latency < 120ms for reranker calls; initial QPS estimate ~ 40 req/s, spike to ~150 for peak events.

Open technical items / asks for Redwood to provide:
1) Recommended SDK/endpoint setup for server-side reranker + embedding flow (examples for Node/Python).
2) Auth guidance: best practice to use short-lived service tokens vs long-lived API key for our infra.
3) Rate limits & quotas guidance: what throttles we should expect on hosted tier and how retries should be handled (429s).
4) Idempotency + request IDs: any advice for deduping and safe retries for mutating requests (if we call tool outputs).
5) Sample MAP (mutual action plan) and POC timeline — we’re aiming for a 4-week POC.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to send technical notes (SDK snippets, retry patterns) by EOD today.
- Redwood to share a short MAP and example config for rate limits and backoff.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (SE + infra) next week — Alex/Priya, what time windows work for you?

I’ve attached the draft MA plan and a high-level architecture diagram for reference.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme discovery call — technical notes on rate limits & retries

Alex / Priya — following up with the technical guidance Marissa requested. High-level + practical config you can try in your POC.

1) SDK & auth
- Use our server SDK (node/python) for the reranker + embeddings flow. For server-to-server calls we recommend a short-lived service token issued via your secrets manager (rotate nightly) or a scoped service account tied to your project. Long-lived API keys are OK for quick POCs but not recommended for production.
- Example (Node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({endpoint: 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1', auth: process.env.REDWOOD_SVC_TOKEN});

2) Routing & fallbacks
- Configure primary region (us-west) and fallback to cross-region for capacity. Use our routing policy: latency-first for user-facing reranking, cost-first for async batch jobs.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- When using tool calling / structured output, include a request-level idempotency-key header for any request that might trigger side-effects. Tool calling responses can be validated against Redwood's JSON schema support (we can pre-register output schemas to ensure stability).

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Pipeline: (a) candidate generation from your existing BM25/semantic index, (b) batch embeddings call for candidates, (c) dot-product similarity, (d) lightweight model reranker for top N (N=10).
- For embeddings, batch up to 512 vectors per request for throughput; monitor memory on client side.

5) Rate limits, retries, and idempotency (the ask):
- Hosted limits (default): 200 requests/minute per API key for synchronous generate endpoints; embeddings have higher throughput limits but are rate-limited by tokens/sec. We’ll provide exact numbers per plan in the MAP.
- 429 handling: treat 429 as transient. Use exponential backoff with full jitter. Example backoff: base=200ms, cap=10s, max_attempts=5.
  Retry pseudo:
    attempt = 0
    while (attempt < max_attempts) {
      resp = call_api();
      if (!resp.status || resp.status != 429) return resp;
      wait = min(cap, base * 2^attempt) * random(0,1)
      sleep(wait)
      attempt++
    }

- Idempotency: For any request that can create/trigger side effects (tool calls, logs to downstream), pass both an Idempotency-Key header and a client-generated request-id. We recommend UUIDv4 per logical action. On duplicate receipt Redwood will return 200+dedup-info, or 409 for conflicting non-idempotent attempts.

- Retries: 
  - Safe to retry on 429 and 503 with backoff.
  - Do NOT retry on 4xx errors other than 429 (e.g., 400/401/403).
  - For streaming responses: if connection fails mid-stream, restart with resume token if you persist token; otherwise treat as new request and include idempotency-key to avoid duplication where possible.

6) Observability hooks
- Include x-request-id on every call so you can correlate traces in our Console. We'll show latency per route and per-token cost so you can tune batching.

If helpful I can paste a short Node and Python snippet for exponential backoff + idempotency header; also attaching a one-page rate-limit SLA (rate-limit-sla.xlsx).

  We’ll accept those and surface dedup info in our logs when applicable.
